# Implementation Plan: Codex non-blocking background-task completion surfacing
<!-- ralph-meta {"overviewTaskId":"codex-nonblocking-bg-completion-surfacing"} -->

*Generated by `/plan-with-ralph` on 2026-06-10. Ready for `/implement-with-ralph --from-plan <job_dir>/plan.md`.*

## Overview

Give the codex CLI agent (driven through happy-cli's `codex app-server`) Claude-Code-parity
non-blocking background-task UX: the agent spawns a long-running process with a short initial
yield, **ends its turn** (so the operator keeps interacting), and when the process exits its
completion surfaces **asynchronously as a new queued turn** — with NO core-turn-loop interleaving
and the minimum possible codex-fork upstream-canonical edit surface. The feature stays **off by
default** behind an explicit opt-in toggle.

The want-(b) primitive already exists in the fork: `spawn_exit_watcher` queues a synthetic
`<task_notification>` and calls `maybe_start_turn_for_pending_work()` when
`Feature::BackgroundProcessNotification` is enabled and it wins a shared `notified` dedup CAS, and
that wake starts a real `RegularTask` **inside codex-core, below the app-server layer** — so the
completion re-enters the model and emits ordinary turn events that app-server forwards to happy-cli
(LOW-A). The work is therefore: (1) turn the feature on behind a toggle (and its **UnifiedExec
prerequisite** — see below); (2) keep the agent OFF the blocking `await_background_completion` and
all follow-up `write_stdin` for that session so the watcher's CAS fires; (3) close a turn-boundary
wake race with one tiny feature-gated codex seam; (4) wire happy-cli to enable the flags, inject the
spawn-then-end-turn policy via its existing `developerInstructions` path, surface the unsolicited
completion turn safely, and expose a readiness probe; (5) keep a documented happy-cli event-bridge
fallback (LOW-B) for the case where live validation shows the auto-turn does not surface cleanly.

**Post-review refinement (Phase 4):** multi-model review (codex + copilot + a source-verifying
critique) converged on three structural corrections folded into this plan: (a) the spawn-then-end-turn
**policy lives in happy-cli `developerInstructions`**, NOT a codex source edit — shrinking the codex
upstream-canonical surface to a single seam; (b) the watcher path is unreachable unless
`Feature::UnifiedExec` is also enabled (it defaults OFF on Windows), so the toggle must enable/verify
BOTH features; (c) the `on_task_finished` race seam must be inserted only **after `active_turn` is
cleared** (not after the pending-input drain) or it silently no-ops.

### Technical Constraints
- **Minimize codex-fork upstream-canonical conflict surface** (operator standing constraint). After
  the Phase-4 refinement, the ONLY codex upstream-canonical edit is the single feature-gated
  `on_task_finished` re-check seam (+ `// SANDBOX PATCH:` marker + patch-surface row). The model policy
  lives entirely in happy-cli `developerInstructions`. A codex `shell_spec.rs` tool-description tweak is
  a documented LAST RESORT only.
- **Two feature flags required**: `features.unified_exec=true` AND
  `features.background_process_notification=true`. Enabling only the latter is inert (F-007).
- **Mutual exclusion via the shared `notified` flag**: after a fire-and-forget spawn the agent must
  avoid ALL follow-up `write_stdin`/`await_background_completion` for that session pre-completion —
  any of them can claim the CAS and suppress the watcher (F-011).
- **Codex submodule = two commits**: codex-side commit first, then the codexu pointer bump. Local
  builds from a codex worktree may need the `codex-rs-overlay` `package.workspace` re-point dance
  (worktree-local scaffolding, reverted before commit).
- **`on_task_finished` lock + placement discipline**: the new `maybe_start_turn_for_pending_work()`
  call must run AFTER `active_turn` is cleared (~:888-908) and outside the active_turn mutex scope.
- **happy-cli turn correlation**: an unsolicited codex-initiated turn must not resolve a stale
  `pendingTurnCompletion`, and an operator message arriving during such a turn must not hang (F-008).

## Approach

### Architecture
Reuse the existing fork-only async watcher path end-to-end (LOW-A) and add the smallest seam that
closes the only source-confirmed race:

1. **Codex race-proof seam (US-001)** — feature-gated turn-end re-check. Insert exactly one
   `maybe_start_turn_for_pending_work()` call in `on_task_finished`, AFTER `active_turn` is cleared
   (~:888-899) and after the `MaybeContinueIfIdle` apply path (~:900-908), guarded by
   `self.enabled(Feature::BackgroundProcessNotification)`. This drains a `<task_notification>` that
   landed in `idle_pending_input` while a later turn was active. Mark `// SANDBOX PATCH:` and add a
   `patch-surface.md` row. Cover with a regression test (exit-during-active-turn → turn-finish →
   auto-wake) sibling to `background_process_notification_wakes_idle_session`; the test must FAIL if
   the wake is attempted before `active_turn` is cleared. No infinite-loop risk (the helper returns on
   empty queues; `start_task` drains queued items).
2. **Spawn-then-end-turn policy in happy-cli (US-002)** — inject guidance via the existing
   `developerInstructions` thread-config path (`runCodex.ts:~1105`), gated by the new default-off
   setting. The policy: start fire-and-forget work with a short `yield_time_ms`, then END the turn
   WITHOUT a blocking `await_background_completion` and WITHOUT any follow-up `write_stdin` for that
   session; if the model needs the output, retrieve it AFTER it is woken by the completion
   notification (a post-exit `await_background_completion` returns the transcript and no longer
   double-notifies, since the watcher CAS already fired). Codex `shell_spec.rs` tool-description edits
   are a documented LAST RESORT only.
3. **Enablement (US-003)** — when the toggle is on, pass BOTH `-c features.unified_exec=true` and
   `-c features.background_process_notification=true` to the spawned app-server, in BOTH the stdio and
   ws spawn paths, gated by the default-off setting (mirroring `mcpNotificationRouting.enabled`). Add
   explicit **unsolicited-active-turn tracking**: before `sendTurnAndWait`, if `_turnId` is active with
   no `pendingTurnCompletion`, either wait for the unsolicited turn to complete before dispatching the
   queued user message, or steer and wait on the active turn id — so an operator message during an
   unsolicited completion turn cannot hang (F-008).
4. **Doctor readiness probe (US-004)** — extend `codexDaemonDoctor.ts` to report a concrete contract:
   (a) the happy async-completion setting state; (b) whether the spawned app-server argv includes both
   feature flags; (c) whether `UnifiedExec`/ConPTY is actually active (so `exec_command` is
   model-visible — fail loudly if not); (d) whether the async-completion `developerInstruction` is
   present; and a human-readable reason when async completion will NOT fire.
5. **Happy-cli LOW-B (conditional fallback, US-006)** — ONLY if US-005 decides
   `low-b-required`. Step 1 (mandatory): define the background/subscribed discriminator by preserving
   `process_id`/`source` through the happy-cli `exec_command_end` mapping (`codexAppServerClient.ts:583`)
   — without it the negative case (foreground completion must NOT loop back) is unverifiable (F-006).
   Step 2: a unified-exec completion consumer analogous to `mcpNotificationConsumer` that pushes a
   synthesized prompt into `MessageQueue2` via a SEPARATE background-process route (never overloading
   `mcpNotificationRouting` kinds).

**Single producer invariant:** the completion turn is produced by codex's `input_queue` (LOW-A). If
LOW-B is taken, codex auto-wake is disabled for that path so exactly one producer remains — never both
(no double prompt).

### Implementation Strategy
Order: codex seam + test (US-001) and happy-cli enablement/policy/doctor (US-002, US-003, US-004,
disjoint repo) can be coded in parallel → mandatory LIVE validation gate (US-005) against a codex
build with the seam + a happy-cli build with the toggle → conditional LOW-B (US-006) only if US-005
decides `low-b-required`. Codex must reach `cargo check --workspace` green + the new `codex-core` test
passing before the codexu pointer bump; happy-cli must reach `tsc --noEmit` + `vitest run` green.

## Scope

### In Scope
- Codex: feature-gated `on_task_finished` turn-end re-check seam (placed after `active_turn` cleared) +
  regression test + `// SANDBOX PATCH:` marker + patch-surface.md row.
- Codex: enable `Feature::BackgroundProcessNotification` AND `Feature::UnifiedExec` via config (no
  source change to turn on).
- Happy-cli: default-off setting; spawn-then-end-turn policy via gated `developerInstructions`; pass
  both `-c` flags in both spawn paths; unsolicited-active-turn tracking; doctor readiness contract;
  targeted vitest coverage.
- Happy-cli LOW-B (fallback, ONLY if US-005 decides required): discriminator-preserving mapping +
  unified-exec completion consumer → `MessageQueue2` via a separate route.
- Mandatory live end-to-end validation (US-005) that emits a structured decision artifact.

### Out of Scope
- Core session/turn-loop interleaving (D-003 / HIGH). Explicitly ruled out.
- A new explicit non-blocking tool/param + result-retrieval tool + per-process mode bit (D-002 /
  MEDIUM). Documented escalation only — build only if instruction-only discipline proves unreliable in
  live validation; do NOT build first.
- Enriching the `<task_notification>` payload beyond `process_id` + `exit_code` (open question; the
  refined policy instead allows a post-notification retrieval call).
- Editing codex tool descriptions in `shell_spec.rs` (LAST RESORT only; not part of the committed path).

## Risk Areas
- **UnifiedExec prerequisite (F-007).** Without `features.unified_exec=true` the watcher path is
  unreachable and the feature silently no-ops on Windows. The doctor probe must surface this.
- **Seam placement no-op (F-009).** Inserting the re-check before `active_turn` is cleared makes it a
  permanent no-op; the regression test must guard placement.
- **happy-cli turn-correlation hang (F-008).** An operator message during an unsolicited completion
  turn can leave a `sendTurnAndWait` promise unresolved → 10-min timeout, unless US-003 tracks
  unsolicited active turns. This is the KEY risk that decides LOW-A vs LOW-B.
- **Model discipline is policy-dependent (F-011).** Multiple dedup-claim sites (await @ `:779-780`,
  any write_stdin observing exit @ `:677-679`, exited stores @ `:722-724`/`:807-808`) can suppress the
  watcher; the policy must steer the model off ALL follow-up await/write_stdin. Reliability is what
  US-005 measures; D-002 hard-guard is the documented escalation.
- **Minimal payload (F-010).** The wake carries only `process_id`+`exit_code`; the policy must permit a
  post-notification retrieval so the agent can act.
- **LOW-B discriminator (F-006).** The happy-cli `exec_command_end` mapping drops `process_id`/`source`;
  LOW-B cannot discriminate foreground vs background without first preserving them.
- **Coalescing/ordering (F-005).** Codex coalesces adjacent background notifications; AC4 must reflect
  the real coalescing + ordering behavior.
- **Cross-repo / submodule mechanics.** Two-commit submodule flow + the overlay re-point dance for
  local codex builds (revert before commit).

## Acceptance Criteria
1. **LOW-A live validation.** With BOTH `features.unified_exec=true` and
   `features.background_process_notification=true` in a LIVE happy-cli codex session: the agent spawns a
   long `exec_command` with a short yield, ends the turn, and does NOT call
   `await_background_completion`; observers confirm (a) the turn ends BEFORE process exit, (b) an
   operator message is processed while the process is still running, (c) on exit the completion surfaces
   as a NEW turn in happy-cli WITHOUT any manual prompt injection, and (d) an operator message sent
   WHILE the unsolicited completion turn is active is handled without a hung `sendTurnAndWait` (no
   timeout). (Validates LOW-A; UnifiedExec prerequisite included.)
2. **Codex regression test.** A background process that exits WHILE a later turn is active still wakes a
   follow-up turn after that turn finishes; the test asserts the wake fires only AFTER `active_turn` is
   cleared (placement guard) and FAILS if the seam is placed before the clear. Passes via
   `cargo test -p codex-core` / `just test -p codex-core`.
3. **No foreground loop-back.** A foreground `exec_command_end` does NOT loop back into the model as a
   fresh prompt — only background/subscribed sessions wake a turn. Under LOW-A this holds because codex
   only wakes via the watcher path; under LOW-B it is verified using the `process_id`/`source`
   discriminator added in US-006.
4. **Ordering + coalescing.** When an operator turn is active and one or more background completions
   land: the active operator turn completes first, then the queued background notifications start ONE
   synthetic turn (coalesced when adjacent, per the codex coalescing path); multiple completions
   preserve enqueue order. Covered by a codex unit/integration test.
5. **Off-by-default observable invariants.** With the setting omitted/disabled: no
   `-c features.unified_exec` and no `-c features.background_process_notification` in the spawned argv
   (both stdio AND ws paths); no async-completion `developerInstruction` appended; no background-completion
   consumer active; existing app-server argv + turn-completion unit tests remain green.
6. **Minimal codex surface.** Codex upstream-canonical edits limited to the one feature-gated
   `on_task_finished` seam (+ marker + patch-surface row). The `shell_spec.rs` tweak is NOT used unless
   explicitly escalated. `cargo check --workspace` (Phase-5a gate) green; the new codex test passes.
7. **Doctor readiness contract.** `happy codex doctor`/status reports: the happy async-completion
   setting state; whether the spawned app-server argv includes both feature flags; whether
   UnifiedExec/ConPTY is actually active (exec_command model-visible); whether the async-completion
   developerInstruction is present; and a human-readable reason when async completion will NOT fire.
8. **Happy-cli tests green.** `tsc --noEmit` and `vitest run` pass, INCLUDING new cases: default-off
   appends no extra `-c` (both stdio + ws paths); opt-in appends both `-c` flags (both paths); an
   unsolicited `turn/started`+`turn/completed` does NOT resolve a stale `pendingTurnCompletion`; doctor
   readiness reporting.

## Preliminary Story Decomposition
- **US-001 (codex):** feature-gated `on_task_finished` turn-end re-check seam (placed after
  `active_turn` cleared) + regression test (placement-guarded) + marker + patch-surface row.
- **US-002 (happy-cli):** spawn-then-end-turn model policy via gated `developerInstructions` injection
  (forbid pre-completion await/write_stdin; allow post-notification retrieval); codex tool-description
  edit is last-resort only.
- **US-003 (happy-cli):** enablement — pass both `-c` flags in both spawn paths gated by the default-off
  setting + unsolicited-active-turn tracking + argv/stale-promise tests.
- **US-004 (happy-cli):** `happy codex doctor`/status readiness contract.
- **US-005 (validation):** mandatory LIVE end-to-end validation emitting a structured decision artifact;
  decides LOW-A sufficiency vs LOW-B.
- **US-006 (happy-cli, CONDITIONAL):** LOW-B — define the `process_id`/`source` discriminator + mapping
  first, then a unified-exec completion consumer → `MessageQueue2` separate route. Implemented ONLY if
  US-005 decides `low-b-required`.

## Suggested Decomposition

Cluster by repo + dependency. The codex cluster and the happy-cli cluster touch disjoint repos and can
be CODED in parallel, but the live-validation gate depends on BOTH, and the LOW-B fallback depends on
the gate's outcome. NOTE for the lead: this is a **dual-repo plan** — `/implement-with-ralph` generates
one PRD per repo, so the codex cluster and happy-cli cluster should be driven as **separate impl jobs**
(or serialized), not a single `--parallel` run across repos.

### Cluster: codex-core-seam
- Stories: US-001
- Phase: 1
- Depends on: None
- File-overlap evidence: shared=[]; exclusive=[`core/src/tasks/mod.rs`, `core/src/unified_exec/process_manager_tests.rs`, `codex/docs/implementation/patch-surface.md`]; risk=low
- `execution_mode` rationale: A single codex-submodule story; runs as its own codex impl job. No same-repo sibling to conflict with after the policy moved to happy-cli.

### Cluster: happy-cli-enablement-and-policy
- Stories: US-002, US-003, US-004
- Phase: 1
- Depends on: None (code); live validation in Phase 2 depends on the codex cluster
- File-overlap evidence: shared=[`src/codex/runCodex.ts`, new default-off setting module]; exclusive=[`src/codex/codexAppServerClient.ts`, `src/codex/codexDaemonDoctor.ts`, `src/codex/codexAppServerClient.test.ts`]; risk=medium (three stories share runCodex.ts + the setting module)
- `execution_mode` rationale: All happy-cli, disjoint repo from the codex cluster, so codeable in parallel with Phase 1 codex work; the three stories share `runCodex.ts` and the setting module so keep them in ONE happy-cli impl job (serial within the job).

### Cluster: live-validation-gate
- Stories: US-005
- Phase: 2
- Depends on: codex-core-seam, happy-cli-enablement-and-policy
- File-overlap evidence: shared=[]; exclusive=[`.ralph/jobs/<job>/low-a-validation.json`]; risk=low
- `execution_mode` rationale: End-to-end validation against a codex build with the seam + a happy-cli build with the toggle; emits a structured decision artifact that gates the conditional LOW-B cluster.

### Cluster: happy-cli-low-b-fallback
- Stories: US-006
- Phase: 3

- File-overlap evidence: shared=[`src/codex/runCodex.ts`, `src/codex/codexAppServerClient.ts` (mapping), `MessageQueue2` route]; exclusive=[new unified-exec completion-consumer module]; risk=low
- `execution_mode` rationale: CONDITIONAL — implemented only if the validation gate decides `low-b-required`; serialized after the gate. Single-producer invariant: if built, codex auto-wake is disabled for this path so there is no double prompt.

## Open Questions
1. **Authoritative producer** for the completion turn — codex `input_queue` (LOW-A) is the committed
   choice; if LOW-B is taken, exactly one producer is wired (codex auto-wake disabled), never both.
   Confirmed at the validation gate.
2. **Notification payload richness** — the wake carries only `process_id`+`exit_code`. The refined
   policy permits a post-notification, already-exited `await_background_completion` retrieval so the
   agent can act; enriching the payload remains out of scope, and a separate retrieval tool is the
   D-002 escalation. [INFERRED default: minimal payload + post-notification retrieval is enough for the
   LOW tier; revisit only if live validation shows the agent cannot act on the wake.]
3. **Model-discipline strength** — instruction-only via `developerInstructions` (LOW, committed) vs
   hard-guarding the await / write_stdin for subscribed sessions (D-002 escalation). Decided by US-005
   reliability data.
4. **Operator-message-vs-completion ordering** — committed contract (AC4): the active operator turn
   completes first, then queued background completions start one coalesced synthetic turn. Verified by a
   codex test.
5. **Doctor-probe home** — extend `src/codex/codexDaemonDoctor.ts` (confirmed to exist via
   `codexCommand.ts:18`); impl confirms the cleanest place to add the readiness fields.
6. **UnifiedExec/ConPTY availability** on the operator's target platform — the doctor probe must
   report when UnifiedExec is unavailable so the user understands why async completion will not fire.
